head: 5b31d95
target: Keep a secret that streams split across text deltas out of what session listeners see, by holding back the newest characters until they can no longer complete a secret.
incidental: the test helper's provider options, which pace the faux model's streaming
the two new stream tests, which measure the fix

questions.prompt: A listener joins the text pieces it receives. Why does the stream hold back the newest characters before sending them?

options.label: Redaction runs on each piece alone, and holding back only delays the marker it inserts.
A secret split across pieces looks clean in each one, so the characters that could still complete it stay unsent.
Pieces can arrive out of order, so the stream waits for the text to be complete before sending.

key_points: a secret split across pieces redacts clean in each piece, but a listener joins the pieces and sees it whole
the stream redacts the held text and the new piece joined, so a secret is caught once both pieces arrived
a secret still forming can only start inside the held window, so the text sent before the window is safe
the window is one character less than the longest secret, the least that covers every secret still forming

questions.prompt: The user aborts mid-reply while the stream is still holding characters back. What does the listener see?

options.label: Only what was already sent. The held characters are lost with the abort.
Every character the transcript kept, delivered when the message ends.
The held characters with any unfinished secret replaced by a marker.
Nothing new. The held characters flush at the start of the next prompt.

key_points: the agent library ends every assistant message with a message end event, finished, errored, or aborted
that event flushes the held characters, so the listener receives every character the transcript kept
an unfinished secret is plain text, so the flush sends it unchanged, with no marker

questions.prompt: One reply arrives as two text blocks. A secret starts in the first block and completes early in the second. The reply also has an emoji. Which of these are true?

options.label: The held characters flush when the first block ends, before the second block starts.
No sent piece ends between the two halves of the emoji.
The rest of the second block waits for the reply to end before it is sent.
The listener never sees either piece of the secret.

key_points: the hold spans the whole message, so a secret piece crossing blocks stays held until the secret completes
the flush keys on the message end, the one boundary that always comes, not on a block end
a cut that would split the two halves of a character moves back one character
text after the completed secret streams out as it arrives, and only the newest window waits
